summary: The design should build on `parrot.auth`, but several contracts are underspecified at security and persistence boundaries. The largest risks are principal confusion, silent durable-store failure, missing start-time PBAC, and process-local notification delivery.

suggestions.title: Make principal binding explicit in OAuth state
suggestions.rationale: `AbstractOAuth2Manager` currently stores `channel` and `user_id`, while Jira’s sink separately infers `extra.nav_user_id`. Introduce an explicit principal reference containing `nav_user_id`, `channel`, and `channel_user_id`; bind it at flow start, verify it at callback, and fail closed when unresolved. This prevents identity changes or ambiguous channel IDs from attaching a grant to the wrong user.

suggestions.title: Do not silently succeed when durable persistence fails
suggestions.rationale: The generic manager catches vault-write failures and continues with Redis, while Jira catches sink failures after writing Redis. That can report a successful connection which is unavailable after cache expiry and contradicts Identity Vault ownership. Callback success should require durable persistence, or explicitly record a pending/degraded state with retry and a non-success UI response.

suggestions.title: Resolve account cardinality before changing keys
suggestions.rationale: The Identity Vault can hold multiple provider accounts, but `UsersIntegrationRow`, persistence, and generic vault names are keyed by only `(user, provider)`, and Jira selects the first accessible resource. Either explicitly make v1 single-account-per-provider and replace on reconnect, or add `account_id` to storage, listing, status, revoke, and callback-selection contracts. The proposed provider-only DELETE endpoint is otherwise ambiguous.

suggestions.title: Enforce PBAC on connect and revoke, not only listing
suggestions.rationale: `IntegrationsService.list_for_user` performs PBAC checks, but `start_connect` validates only origin and registry membership; the handler passes the request nowhere for policy evaluation. The accepted mitigation explicitly requires provider/scope allowlists, so user-level start, reconnect, and disconnect routes must evaluate PBAC with the requested scopes before creating OAuth state or deleting credentials.

suggestions.title: Separate connection ownership from agent capability enablement
suggestions.rationale: The current UI calls `confirmIntegrationEnable` after OAuth, and that service writes `user_agent_toolkits`; persistence documentation says those rows drive agent hydration. Removing the table or endpoint as part of the connection reversal can silently remove tools. Keep connection state principal-scoped, then define a separate capability/policy mechanism for which agents may use it; update both `IntegrationsMenu` and `ConnectIntegrationPill` to stop requiring agent enablement only after that mechanism exists.

suggestions.title: Define cross-process notifier delivery explicitly
suggestions.rationale: `setup_event_fanout` configures a publish-only Streams bus with no consumers, and `UserSocketManager` keeps sockets in process-local maps. Existing Telegram and Teams notifiers are held on the local aiohttp app. A core registry alone cannot deliver a callback from one worker to a channel adapter in another process; use an idempotent Redis/outbox delivery queue or constrain and verify same-process deployment.

suggestions.title: Distinguish invalid refresh tokens from transient refresh failures
suggestions.rationale: The generic refresh path converts `aiohttp.ClientError` into `PermissionError`, then revokes the credential on any `PermissionError`. A temporary provider/network failure can therefore delete a valid grant. Add a typed invalid-grant outcome, revoke only for confirmed provider rejection, and emit `refresh_failed` without destructive revocation for transport errors.

suggestions.title: Use a superset needs-auth contract
suggestions.rationale: `AuthorizationRequired` carries tool name, scopes, and message, while `CredentialRequired` additionally carries `auth_kind`, device code, verification URI, and expiry. Mapping both to the current `ToolResult` metadata or `AuthRequiredEnvelope` would discard device-code UX data. Define one typed payload with optional surface-specific fields, then make ToolManager and AgentTalk serialize the same payload.

suggestions.title: Make MCP credential resolution genuinely per-call
suggestions.rationale: `add_oauth_mcp_server` still requires a `user_id`, but the factory does not put it into the resulting config. Separately, broker injection occurs only when `inject_broker_credential` is enabled and the call ContextVar is populated; merely removing the parameter will not establish user isolation. Define a context-aware token supplier or header provider that resolves the principal through the broker on every call, and keep MCP OAuth transport state separate from broker credentials.

suggestions.title: Keep provider-specific behavior typed before introducing YAML hooks
suggestions.rationale: The existing registry requires a manager and toolkit factory, while Jira and O365 implement provider-specific exchange and identity logic in code. A descriptor field containing a post-exchange hook name creates dynamic dispatch, validation, and security problems before the lifecycle contract is stable. Start with a typed Pydantic descriptor for metadata, endpoints, scopes, and refresh policy; retain explicit manager subclasses for exchange/discovery until at least two providers share a proven hook model.

suggestions.title: Require a migration and isolation contract matrix before cutover
suggestions.rationale: Existing tests cover Identity Vault status, sink lookup behavior, O365 refresh, and AuthorizationRequired, but not principal-keyed dual reads, cross-channel reuse, unlinked-user rejection, legacy-key deletion, concurrent users, notifier failure, or CredentialRequired serialization. Add tests that prove a channel cannot read another principal’s token and that callback success is impossible without the required durable write.
